slides.title: Synchronizing Threads to Prevent Race Conditions
slides.prompt: When multiple threads access shared mutable state, race conditions can occur. Synchronization primitives like `Lock`, `RLock` (reentrant lock), `Semaphore`, and `Event` coordinate thread execution safely.
slides.codeSnippet:
import threading

counter = 0
lock = threading.Lock()

def increment():
    global counter
    with lock:
        # Critical section protected by lock
        counter += 1

threads = [threading.Thread(target=increment) for _ in range(10)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()

slides.title: Difference Between Lock and RLock
slides.prompt: What is the key advantage of an `RLock` (Reentrant Lock) over a standard `Lock`?
options: An RLock can be acquired multiple times by the same thread without causing a deadlock
An RLock executes faster by ignoring GIL boundaries
An RLock automatically releases after a designated timeout
An RLock works across process boundaries instead of thread boundaries
slides.correctAnswer: An RLock can be acquired multiple times by the same thread without causing a deadlock

slides.title: Purpose of threading.Event
slides.prompt: How does `threading.Event` facilitate communication between threads?
options: One thread signals an event, while other threads wait for the internal flag to become true using `wait()`
It acts as a bounded queue for transferring high-throughput data
It automatically cancels long-running background tasks after a timer
It balances CPU load dynamically across available physical cores
slides.correctAnswer: One thread signals an event, while other threads wait for the internal flag to become true using wait()

slides.title: Understanding Semaphores
slides.prompt: What defines the functionality of a `Semaphore` in thread management?
options: It manages an internal counter restricting resource access to a maximum fixed number of concurrent threads
It locks a file handle exclusively on the OS filesystem
It forces threads to execute in alphabetical order based on thread name
It raises an exception if more than one thread is created
slides.correctAnswer: It manages an internal counter restricting resource access to a maximum fixed number of concurrent threads
